## Verdict: REJECT (three diff-added prose claims are false against HEAD; one checklist FAIL)

## Issue Compliance
Reviewed against issue #2035: Add a telemetry.enabled master config key that turns off PRFlow's optional telemetry in one switch — criteria from workpad; scope unchanged. Requirement-based checklist items are included in the verification results below.
Criteria came from the `/prflow:implement` workpad comment — this run's authoritative set, possibly narrowed from the issue.
No divergence between the workpad's criteria and the issue body's.

All eight acceptance criteria are met by the shipped behavior. The focused module `lib/test/run-module.sh efficiency-trace-telemetry` ran clean this iteration: 1051 passed, 0 failed. AC8 (no `skills/**`, no `.github/workflows/**` change) holds — the cached diff carries zero sections under either path.

## Verification Checklist Results
12 passed, 1 failed, 0 inconclusive — 1 via lite probe, 12 via agent.
- VC-9: FAIL — the `scripts/telemetry-master-off.py` docstring asserts that `config-get.sh` and `lib/efficiency-trace.sh` carry "byte-equivalent" inline `python3 -c` copies; they are not byte-equivalent (`PRFLOW_TEL_CFG` vs `DEVFLOW_TEL_CFG`) [scripts/telemetry-master-off.py:7]

## Code Review Findings

### Important / Major
1. The `telemetry-master-off.py` docstring calls the two inline `python3 -c` copies "byte-equivalent"; they differ in the environment-variable name (`PRFLOW_TEL_CFG` in `config-get.sh`, `DEVFLOW_TEL_CFG` in `efficiency-trace.sh`), and neither is byte-equivalent to the module's own `telemetry_master_off()`. The instruction "Change one, change all three" is correct; the descriptor is not. (raised by 1/3 agents, corroborated by checklist VC-9) [self-contradicting-diff carve-out: scripts/telemetry-master-off.py]
2. The "every optional telemetry mechanism" universal survives in the two summary rows a reader scans first — `docs/external/docs/configuration/observability-and-privacy.md:14` and `docs/internal/DEVFLOW_SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md:1146` — while the same diff adds and retains the carve-out that `prflow.execution_transcript_artifact_enabled` is deliberately not enrolled. The prose bodies already say "enrolled" and are correct; the rows were not swept. (raised by 2/3 agents) [self-contradicting-diff carve-out: docs/external/docs/configuration/observability-and-privacy.md]
3. Six diff-added description lines state the inheritance condition as "when this key is absent", but an enrolled sub-key present as JSON `null` also inherits the master: `emit_default_or_fail` fires on an empty resolved value and the walker cannot distinguish present-null from absent. Verified against HEAD — with `{"telemetry":{"enabled":false},"prflow":{"execution_diagnostics_enabled":null}}` the resolver prints `false`. The sibling `probe_superseded_key` in the same file deliberately does distinguish present-null. Either narrow the gate to genuine absence or correct the six lines. (raised by 1/3 agents) [self-contradicting-diff carve-out: scripts/config-get.sh]
4. `scripts/telemetry-master-off.py` collapses "telemetry is on" and "I could not determine anything" onto exit 1, so `collect-staged-telemetry.sh` announces only two of three unconsulted-master causes: a derived `_CST_CFG` that does not exist, is unreadable, or holds corrupt JSON stages and uploads the payload with no log line at all — the exact failure mode the two existing `master switch was NOT consulted` warnings were added to close, reached by a third route. (raised by 1/3 agents) [suspected over-grade: shape 2 — observable fail-direction is a missing diagnostic breadcrumb on a path that already fails safe to telemetry-on, milder than the Important label]

### Suggestion / Minor
1. `lib/test/modules/efficiency-trace-telemetry.sh:6812` calls `telemetry-master-off.py` "the single-source JSON-boolean-false predicate" while the diff ships three copies and the script's own docstring says "Change one, change all three". A maintainer reading the module header would believe editing the `.py` alone suffices. Capped by the behavior-inert prose cap: no tool parses this comment to decide behavior, and `.github/actions/vendor-plugin/vendor-slice.sh:110` prunes `lib/test` from the vendored slice, so it ships to no consumer — both limbs hold. (raised by 1/3 agents)
2. The `do_persist` gate comment (`lib/efficiency-trace.sh:1534-1539`) is a six-line derivation block mixing the load-bearing exec-edge prohibition with restatement the adjacent `is False` expression already carries; the sibling at `scripts/config-get.sh` has the same shape at four lines. (raised by 1/3 agents)
3. `scripts/collect-staged-telemetry.sh` sources `../lib/resolve-state-dir.sh` with `2>/dev/null || true` and falls through to the canonical-only path silently, where `config-get.sh` emits a warning for the byte-identical condition. (raised by 1/3 agents)
4. `"measured at roughly 1-3% of a run"` is a checked-in figure in shipped external docs with no recorded provenance, against the repo's prefer-generated-evidence convention. (raised by 1/3 agents)
5. The enrolled five-key set is a hardcoded `case` with no mechanical coupling to the schema descriptions that name the inheritance; a sixth default-true gate added later would pass every test and silently not inherit. (raised by 1/3 agents)
6. `lib/test/modules/coverage-map.json` leaves `scripts/config-get.sh` at `unmodularized` with an empty note, though it carries the resolver-inheritance change and most of the new assertions. (raised by 1/3 agents)
7. The `.devflow/` read-through fixture stages under `.devflow/tmp/telemetry-stage-*/` while both the producer and the collector glob `.prflow/tmp/telemetry-stage-*/`, so it is not a real positive control for the mid-migration case the gate's comment cites. (raised by 1/3 agents)
8. The `--persist` "python3 absent" breadcrumb has no assertion, where the `collect-staged-telemetry.sh` equivalent has two. (raised by 1/3 agents)
